subject: math
title: Location and Movement: Grid Maps, Directions and Quarter Turns
seo_title: Grade 3 Location and Movement Worksheets: Grid Maps and Turns (Free)
standard_text: Create and interpret simple maps of familiar places
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on location and movement: read grid maps with references like B3, use position words, follow moves on a grid and make quarter and half turns, clockwise and counterclockwise. 100 questions with an answer key, Ontario curriculum aligned and great EQAO practice.
key_big: A grid reference gives the letter (across) first, then the number (down): B3.
key_sub: When you follow moves, count the squares you move, not the square you start on. A quarter turn clockwise goes the same way as the hands of a clock.
body_html:
Grid maps and grid references

A map shows a place from above. Many maps have a grid. The columns have letters across the top. The rows have numbers down the side. A grid reference like B4 names one square.

Go across to the letter first. Then go down to the number.

Example

On the park map, what is in square E2?

Go across to column E. Then go down to row 2.

Answer: the splash pad

Position words

Use words like next to, between, above, below, left of and right of. On the park map, the slide is between the swings and the parking lot. The pond is above the garden.

Follow moves on a grid

Do one move at a time. Count the squares you move. Do not count the square you start on.

Quarter turns and half turns

A quarter turn is one of four equal turns that go all the way around. A half turn is two quarter turns: you face the opposite way. Clockwise turns the same way as the hands of a clock. Counterclockwise turns the other way.

A robot on a grid moves forward the way it faces. When it turns, it stays on the same square.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the column and the row (B4 read as D2)Letter first, across. Then the number, down.
Writing the number first (4B)Always write the letter first: B4.
Counting the starting squareCount the moves, not the square you stand on.
Turning the wrong wayClockwise goes like clock hands: top, right, bottom, left.
Making a quarter turn for a half turnA half turn is two quarter turns. You face the opposite way.
Using left and right of the page for a person facing the bottomTurn the map so you face the same way as the person.

faq.q: What do Grade 3 students learn about location and movement in Ontario math?
faq.a: In the Ontario curriculum (Spatial Sense, E1.4), Grade 3 students create and read simple maps of familiar places and give and follow multi-step directions that use distances and quarter and half turns.

faq.q: How do you read a grid reference like B3?
faq.a: Go across to column B first, then down to row 3. The letter always comes first, so B3 is not the same square as C2.

faq.q: What is the difference between a quarter turn and a half turn?
faq.a: A quarter turn is one of four equal turns that go all the way around. A half turn is two quarter turns, so you end up facing the opposite way.

faq.q: Are maps and directions on the Grade 3 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, which includes spatial sense, so questions about maps, position and movement can appear. These worksheets are good practice.

sets.title: Read a grid map: grid references like B3

items.q: What is the grid reference of the splash pad?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The splash pad is in column E, row 2: E2. Write the letter first.

items.q: Which row is the fountain in?
items.e: Rows go across and are named with numbers. The fountain is beside the number 3. It is in column F, the 6th column, but row 3: F3.

items.q: What is in square A3?
items.e: Find column A along the top, then go down to row 3. Square A3 is the garden. Mixing up the column and the row (column C, row 1) gives the swings.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the sandbox?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The sandbox is in column B, row 4: B4. Write the letter first.

items.q: Which column is the bench in?
items.e: Columns go up and down and are named with letters. The bench is under the letter C. Its row is 2, so its grid reference is C2.

items.q: Which squares does the baseball diamond cover?
items.e: The baseball diamond is in the bottom row, row 5, in columns B and C: B5 and C5.

items.q: What is in square D5?
items.e: Find column D along the top, then go down to row 5. Square D5 is the tree. Mixing up the column and the row (column E, row 4) gives the soccer field.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the slide?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The slide is in column D, row 1: D1. Write the letter first.

items.q: Which square is empty?
items.e: B2 is in column B, row 2. Nothing is there. C2 is the bench, B3 is the picnic tables and A2 is the pond.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the gate?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The gate is in column A, row 5: A5. Write the letter first.

items.q: Mei says the sandbox is in square D2. What mistake did she make?
c: she mixed up the column and the row
items.e: The sandbox is in column B (the 2nd column) and row 4: B4. Mei used the 4 as the column (D) and the 2 as the row. Always go across to the letter first, then down to the number.

items.q: What is in square F3?
items.e: Find column F along the top, then go down to row 3. Square F3 is the fountain.

items.q: Which grid reference is not on this map?
items.e: The columns go from A to F and the rows go from 1 to 5. There is no column G, so G2 is not on the map.

items.q: What is in square C1?
items.e: Find column C along the top, then go down to row 1. Square C1 is the swings. Mixing up the column and the row (column A, row 3) gives the garden.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bench?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bench is in column C, row 2: C2. Write the letter first.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the pond?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The pond is in column A, row 2: A2. Write the letter first.

items.q: What is in square B3?
items.e: Find column B along the top, then go down to row 3. Square B3 is the picnic tables. Mixing up the column and the row (column C, row 2) gives the bench.

items.q: The parking lot covers two squares. What are they?
items.e: The parking lot is in row 1, in columns E and F. Letter first: E1 and F1.

items.q: Which square in row 5 is empty?
items.e: Look along row 5: A5 is the gate, B5 and C5 are the baseball diamond, D5 is the tree, E5 is empty and F5 is the bike rack.

items.q: How many squares does the soccer field cover on the map?
items.e: The soccer field is 2 squares across and 2 squares down: D3, E3, D4 and E4. That is 4 squares.

sets.title: Position words: next to, between, above, below, left and right

items.q: What is between the office and the library?
items.e: Find the office and the library. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the front doors.

items.q: What is in the top right corner of the map?
items.e: Top means the top row. Right means the right side. The music room is in the top right corner. The parking lot is in the top left.

items.q: Ava stands in square B3 and faces the bottom of the map. Is the garden on her left or her right?
items.e: Ava faces the bottom of the map, the opposite way to you. Her left and right are swapped. Turn the page upside down to check: the garden (A3) is on her right.

items.q: What is just above the play structure on the map?
items.e: Look one square up from the play structure. It is the garden. The basketball court is below it, not above.

items.q: Which place is next to the gym?
items.e: The front doors touch the top of the gym. The portable, the library and the garden do not touch it: there is a gap.

items.q: How many squares do you move from the front doors, straight down the map, to the field?
items.e: From the front doors (D1) go down: D2 is 1, D3 is 2 and the field (D4) is 3. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Which of these places is closest to the front doors?
items.e: The gym is right below the front doors, 1 square away. The portable is 3 squares away and the others are further.

items.q: Which place is next to the bench?
items.e: Next to means touching, side by side. The field is just to the left of the bench. The sandbox and the portable are 2 squares away.

items.q: What is just below the office on the map?
items.e: Look one square down from the office. That square is part of the gym. The parking lot is on the left of the office.

items.q: What is just to the right of the basketball court on the map?
items.e: Look one square to the right of the basketball court. It is part of the field.

items.q: Amira stands in square B3 and faces the top of the map. Is the garden on her left or her right?
items.e: Amira faces the top of the map, the same way you look at the page. The garden (A3) is on the left side of B3, so it is on her left.

items.q: How many squares do you move from the bike rack, straight to the right, to the gym?
items.e: From the bike rack (A2) go right: B2 is 1 and the gym (C2) is 2. Do not count the bike rack square.

items.q: The field is ___ the gym.
items.e: The field and the gym share columns C and D. The field is lower on the map, so it is below the gym.

items.q: What is in the bottom left corner of the map?
items.e: Bottom means the bottom row. Left means the left side. The basketball court is in the bottom left corner. The play structure is just above it.

items.q: The library is ___ the front doors.
items.e: The library is in the same row as the front doors, one square to the right.

items.q: What is just to the left of the library on the map?
items.e: Look one square to the left of the library. It is the front doors. The music room is on its right.

items.q: The garden is next to two places. What are they?
c: the bike rack and the parking lot
the bike rack and the play structure
the play structure and the basketball court
items.e: Look at the squares touching the garden: the bike rack is just above it and the play structure is just below it. The square on its right is empty.

items.q: What is between the bike rack and the play structure?
items.e: Find the bike rack and the play structure. They are in the same column. The place in the middle of them is the garden.

items.q: What is just above the art room on the map?
items.e: Look one square up from the art room. It is the music room, in the top row.

items.q: What is between the parking lot and the front doors?
items.e: Find the parking lot and the front doors. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the office.

sets.title: Follow moves on a grid: right, left, up and down

items.q: Start at the fountain. Move 2 squares down, then 2 squares left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F3. Go 2 squares down to F5, then 2 squares left to D5. The tree is in D5.

items.q: Start at the sandbox. Move 2 squares up, then 1 square right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at B4. Go 2 squares up to B2, then 1 square right to C2. The bench is in C2.

items.q: How many squares to the right is it from the gate to the tree?
items.e: The gate is in A5 and the tree is in D5. Count the moves: 3 squares right. Do not count the gate square.

items.q: Start at the pond. Move 2 squares right, then 1 square up. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A2. Go 2 squares right to C2, then 1 square up to C1. The swings are in C1.

items.q: Benjamin starts on the red dot. He moves 2 squares left, then 3 squares up. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E4. Go 2 squares left to C4, then 3 squares up to C1. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Start at the bike rack. Move 3 squares up, then 1 square left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 3 squares up to F2, then 1 square left to E2. The splash pad is in E2.

items.q: Aiden starts on the red dot. He moves 2 squares down, then 3 squares right. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at B1. Go 2 squares down to B3, then 3 squares right to E3. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Zoe starts on the red dot. She moves 3 squares right. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at B4. Go 3 squares right to E4. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Jayden starts on the red dot. He moves 1 square up, then 3 squares left. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 1 square up to F4, then 3 squares left to C4. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Which moves take you from the pond to the sandbox?
items.e: The pond is in A2 and the sandbox is in B4. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 1 square right, then 2 squares down.

items.q: Start at the gate. Move 2 squares up, then 1 square right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 2 squares up to A3, then 1 square right to B3. The picnic tables are in B3.

items.q: Start in the square with the bike rack. Move 2 squares left, then 3 squares up. Which square do you land in?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 2 squares left to D5, then 3 squares up to D2.

items.q: How many squares down is it from the swings to the baseball diamond, going straight down?
items.e: The swings are in C1. Go straight down: C2, C3, C4, C5. The baseball diamond is in C5. That is 4 squares down.

items.q: Which moves take you from the gate to the bench?
items.e: The gate is in A5 and the bench is in C2. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 2 squares right, then 3 squares up.

items.q: Olivia starts on the red dot. She moves 3 squares down. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at C1. Go 3 squares down to C4. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Nathan starts on the red dot. He moves 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 3 squares right to D5, then 2 squares up to D3. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Kai starts on the red dot. He moves 3 squares up. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares up to E2. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Which moves take you from the slide to the fountain?
items.e: The slide is in D1 and the fountain is in F3. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on: 2 squares right, then 2 squares down.

items.q: Priya starts on the red dot. She moves 3 squares left. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E2. Go 3 squares left to B2. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Start in the square with the washrooms. Move 3 squares right, then 2 squares down. Which square do you land in?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 3 squares right to D1, then 2 squares down to D3.

sets.title: Quarter turns and half turns: follow and describe a path

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 3 squares forward, make a quarter turn clockwise, then move 2 squares forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at A5, facing up the map. Move 3 squares forward to A2. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face to the right. Move 2 squares forward to C2. That is square A. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on B.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 2 squares forward, make a quarter turn clockwise, then move 3 squares forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at F5, facing to the left. Move 2 squares forward to D5. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face up the map. Move 3 squares forward to D2. That is square D. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on A.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 3 squares forward, make a quarter turn counterclockwise, then move 2 squares forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at E2, facing to the left. Move 3 squares forward to B2. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face down the map. Move 2 squares forward to B4. That is square C. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on A.

items.q: Ethan faces the stage. He makes a quarter turn clockwise, then another quarter turn clockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Ethan starts facing the stage. Clockwise goes the same way as the hands of a clock: top, right, bottom, left. One quarter turn clockwise takes him to the clock, and another takes him to the doors. Two quarter turns make a half turn.

items.q: Emma faces the window. Which turn makes her face the board?
items.e: Clockwise goes top, right, bottom, left. From the window, one quarter turn counterclockwise brings her to the board. A quarter turn the other way would face the door.

items.q: The robot starts facing the way its arrow points. Which steps make it follow the dashed path?
items.e: Start at F2, facing to the left. Move 3 squares forward to C2. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face down the map. Move 2 squares forward to C4. Count the squares the robot moves, not the square it starts on, and check which way it turns.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 2 squares forward, make a quarter turn clockwise, move 2 squares forward, make a quarter turn clockwise, then move 1 square forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at A5, facing up the map. Move 2 squares forward to A3. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face to the right. Move 2 squares forward to C3. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face down the map. Move 1 square forward to C4. That is square B. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on A.

items.q: Leah faces the doors. She makes a half turn. What does she face now?
items.e: Leah starts facing the doors. A half turn is two quarter turns, so she ends up facing the opposite wall: the scoreboard.

items.q: The robot starts facing the way its arrow points. Which steps make it follow the dashed path?
items.e: Start at B1, facing down the map. Move 1 square forward to B2. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face to the right. Move 4 squares forward to F2. Count the squares the robot moves, not the square it starts on, and check which way it turns.

items.q: Noah faces the penalty box. Which turn makes him face the scoreboard?
items.e: Clockwise goes top, right, bottom, left. From the penalty box, one quarter turn clockwise brings him to the scoreboard. A quarter turn the other way would face the doors.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 3 squares forward, make a quarter turn clockwise, move 2 squares forward, make a quarter turn counterclockwise, then move 1 square forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at F1, facing down the map. Move 3 squares forward to F4. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face to the left. Move 2 squares forward to D4. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face down the map. Move 1 square forward to D5. That is square D. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on A.

items.q: Chloe faces the board. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Chloe starts facing the board. Clockwise goes the same way as the hands of a clock: top, right, bottom, left. One quarter turn clockwise from the board is the window.

items.q: Liam faces the door. He makes a quarter turn counterclockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Liam starts facing the door. Counterclockwise goes the other way: top, left, bottom, right. One quarter turn counterclockwise from the door is the window. Turning clockwise by mistake would give the bookshelf.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 2 squares forward, make a quarter turn counterclockwise, then move 3 squares forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at B1, facing down the map. Move 2 squares forward to B3. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face to the right. Move 3 squares forward to E3. That is square B. Counting the starting square as 1 stops the robot short, on A.

items.q: The robot starts facing the way its arrow points. Which steps make it follow the dashed path?
c: Forward 2, half turn, forward 2, quarter turn clockwise, forward 1
Forward 2, quarter turn counterclockwise, forward 2, quarter turn clockwise, forward 1
Forward 2, quarter turn clockwise, forward 2, quarter turn counterclockwise, forward 1
Forward 3, quarter turn counterclockwise, forward 3, quarter turn clockwise, forward 2
items.e: Start at E5, facing up the map. Move 2 squares forward to E3. A quarter turn counterclockwise makes it face to the left. Move 2 squares forward to C3. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face up the map. Move 1 square forward to C2. Count the squares the robot moves, not the square it starts on, and check which way it turns.

items.q: How many quarter turns make a half turn?
items.e: A quarter turn is one of four equal turns that go all the way around. Two quarter turns make a half turn, and a half turn makes you face the opposite way.

items.q: The robot starts facing the way its arrow points. Which steps make it follow the dashed path?
items.e: Start at A5, facing up the map. Move 2 squares forward to A3. A quarter turn clockwise makes it face to the right. Move 3 squares forward to D3. Count the squares the robot moves, not the square it starts on, and check which way it turns.

items.q: Mateo faces the stove. He makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Mateo starts facing the stove. Clockwise goes the same way as the hands of a clock: top, right, bottom, left. One quarter turn clockwise from the stove is the fridge.

items.q: Maya faces the clock. She makes a quarter turn counterclockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Maya starts facing the clock. Counterclockwise goes the other way: top, left, bottom, right. One quarter turn counterclockwise from the clock is the stage. Turning clockwise by mistake would give the doors.

items.q: The robot faces the way its arrow points. It follows these steps: move 4 squares forward, make a half turn, then move 1 square forward. Where does it stop?
items.e: Start at A3, facing to the right. Move 4 squares forward to E3. A half turn makes the robot face the opposite way: to the left. Move 1 square forward to D3. That is square C. Making only a quarter turn instead of a half turn takes it to A.

sets.title: Word problems: find the skating rink and other places

items.q: Zoe walks 3 squares right on a grid, then 3 squares left. Where is she now?
items.e: Left is the opposite of right. 3 squares left undoes 3 squares right, so Zoe is back at the start.

items.q: Mei faces the board. She makes a quarter turn clockwise, then another quarter turn clockwise. What turn did she make in all?
items.e: Two quarter turns the same way make a half turn. Mei now faces the back of the classroom.

items.q: Sofia leaves the community centre. She goes 1 square down, then 1 square right. Where is she?
items.e: Start at D4. Go 1 square down to D5, then 1 square right to E5. The dentist is in E5. Going left instead of right gives the bus stop.

items.q: Which moves take Liam from his house to the school?
items.e: The house is in A5 and the school starts in C1. Go 2 squares right (A to C) and 4 squares up (row 5 to row 1). Count the moves, not the starting square.

items.q: Hana is at the fire station. She walks 3 squares down the map. Where is she now?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 3 squares down to F4. The post office is in F4. Counting the fire station square would stop her at the park.

items.q: Ava writes that the swings on a park map are in square 3B. Which grid reference should she write?
items.e: Write the letter (the column) first, then the number (the row): B3. C2 is a different square.

items.q: Each square on the map stands for 100 m. How far is it from the library, straight to the right, to the school?
items.e: From the library (A1) to the school (C1) is 2 squares. 2 × 100 m = 200 m. Counting the library square too gives 300 m.

items.q: Liam leaves his house and walks 2 squares up the map. What does he reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 2 squares up to A3. The skating rink is in A3. Counting his house as 1 would stop him in A4, an empty square.

items.q: Arjun stands at the bus stop, facing up the map. He walks 1 square forward, makes a quarter turn counterclockwise, then walks 1 square forward. Where is he?
items.e: From the bus stop (C5) one square forward is C4. A quarter turn counterclockwise turns him to face left. One square left is B4: the grocery store. Turning clockwise by mistake gives the community centre.

items.q: Lucas waits at the bus stop, facing the pool (up the map). Then he makes a half turn. Which way does he face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. Up becomes down. A quarter turn would make him face left or right.

items.q: What is in square B4?
items.e: Find column B, then go down to row 4: the grocery store. Mixing up the column and the row (column D, row 2) gives the bakery.

items.q: Owen leaves the café, facing up the map. He walks 2 squares forward, makes a quarter turn clockwise, then walks 1 square forward. Where is he?
items.e: From the café (B3) two squares forward is B1. A quarter turn clockwise turns him to face right. One square right is C1: the school. Turning counterclockwise by mistake gives the library.

items.q: Each square is 100 m. Liam walks from his house to the skating rink and back home again. How far does he walk?
items.e: The house (A5) to the skating rink (A3) is 2 squares, or 200 m. There and back is 200 m + 200 m = 400 m.

items.q: Find the skating rink. What is its grid reference?
items.e: The skating rink is in column A and row 3. Write the letter first: A3. C1 has the column and row mixed up.

items.q: In gym class, the teacher says: “Make a quarter turn to your right.” Which way does Amira turn?
items.e: Turning to your right goes the same way as the hands of a clock, so it is a quarter turn clockwise. Turning to your left is counterclockwise.

items.q: Each square is 100 m. Liam walks from his house 2 squares up to the skating rink, then 2 squares right to the pool. How far does he walk in all?
items.e: Up to the rink is 2 squares and over to the pool is 2 more: 2 + 2 = 4 squares. 4 × 100 m = 400 m.

items.q: The class goes skating on a field trip. Which moves take them from the school (C1) to the skating rink?
items.e: The school is in C1 and the skating rink is in A3. Go 2 squares left (C to A) and 2 squares down (row 1 to row 3).

items.q: On a map, each square stands for 10 m. A bike path is 6 squares long on the map. How long is the real bike path?
items.e: Each square is 10 m, so 6 squares is 6 × 10 m = 60 m. Adding 6 + 10 = 16 does not work.

items.q: What is between the skating rink and the pool?
items.e: The skating rink (A3), the café (B3) and the pool (C3) are in row 3. The café is in the middle.

items.q: Each square is 100 m. How far is it from the bus stop straight up to the pool?
items.e: From the bus stop (C5) up to the pool (C3) is 2 squares. 2 × 100 m = 200 m.
